headline: Scientists Name Stunning New Coral After Tolkien's Elvish Language
meta_description: A brilliant yellow coral discovered off Costa Rica was so unique that scientists created an entirely new family to classify it, naming it after Tolkien's Elvis…
summary_short: A meter-tall golden coral discovered off Costa Rica proved so genetically distinctive that researchers established a new coral family to classify it.
body:
Marine scientists surveying underwater mountains off Costa Rica have identified a remarkable golden coral so unlike any known species that researchers had to create an entirely new coral family to classify it. The bright yellow, tree-like coral—named Laurinque elenya, drawing inspiration from J.R.R. Tolkien's Elvish language—grows over a meter tall on seamounts between 360 and 529 meters below the Pacific's surface. The discovery was made during expeditions in 2019 and 2023 aboard research vessels operated by the Schmidt Ocean Institute, with specimens collected using a remotely operated vehicle called SuBastian.

What makes this coral truly exceptional isn't just its vivid appearance. When scientists initially tried to classify it using three genes commonly used for coral identification, each gene suggested a different, unrelated family—an unusually confusing result. Only when researchers deployed phylogenomics, comparing hundreds of genes simultaneously, did the picture become clear: this coral belongs to no previously recognized family. It represents its own distinct evolutionary lineage, closest to Eunicellidae but different enough to warrant the creation of a new family, Laurinqueidae.

The coral's scientific name reflects the enchanting deep-sea landscape where it thrives. Laurinque means "golden tree" in Quenya, Tolkien's Elvish language, while elenya means "stellar" or "of the stars." The latter reference captures how the coral colonies rise from rocky seafloor outcrops nearly covered by brittle stars, creating what Dr. Odalisca Breedy, lead researcher from the Universidad de Costa Rica, described as an "almost mystical elvish landscape." This discovery underscores how Earth's deep ocean—covering roughly two-thirds of the planet—remains vastly unexplored, with coral gardens like this one serving as vital biodiversity centers for countless deep-sea species.
quick_facts: Discovered 360-529 meters below the Pacific Ocean off Costa Rica
Named Laurinque elenya using Tolkien's Elvish language for 'golden tree of the stars'
Grows more than one meter tall in tree-like colonies
Scientists created entirely new coral family Laurinqueidae to classify it
Phylogenomic analysis of hundreds of genes revealed its unique evolutionary lineage
